_comment: GENERATED by tools/dump_steal_relbranch.py -- do not hand-edit.
For every function with a committed trampoline steal length: does the stolen byte range
contain a PC-RELATIVE call or jump? mh::hook::install_trampoline copies those bytes
verbatim to a new address and relocates nothing, so a relative branch inside them
branches by the original displacement from the new address the first time it runs.
tools/gen_dll_effects.py REFUSES to gate a target flagged here, and refuses to run at
all if a target it wants to gate is MISSING from this file -- fail-closed, so adding a
new target forces a refresh rather than silently inheriting no answer.
Found by TACT-CUT2: a gate over llm_math_atan (12 bytes, steal 9 = FLD + CALL rel32)
sent every tactical atan to a wrong address. The mission ended after frame 1 with no
crash dump, and --tact-determinism reported '0 frames', which reads like a scenario
problem and says nothing about a bad hook. See docs/dead-ends.md.
